title: fix(plugin-auth): the last-administrator guard answers a read fault 503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE, the code its sibling guards answer with
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-tesla"} -->
_Requested by **Tesla** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao?thread=cmsg_01AXsQkLFKRdQCqQ3RTr6Jao2WtPchvUshT9LuGkEhb1h3)_

Fixes #25364

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## Measured first: the shared shape, not one half

The card asked whether to change one half of the last-administrator guard or the shared `failClosed` shape. Measured on `main` at d12e650de:

- Every half that judges a write (`enforce` for the two `sys_user` halves, `enforceStanding` for the membership, grant, activation-ledger and organization halves, and `judgeOrganizationDelete`) runs inside `failClosed`, which answered a read fault with `refuse()`: 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`.
- The Default Organization slug-capture rule (`guardOrganizationDefaultSlug`, from #25286) does **not** use `failClosed`. It has its own `catch`, which also answered 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`.
- So changing the slug rule alone would have split the guard: a read fault on the slug-capture rule would answer 503 while the same fault on the update half of the same `organization/update` request answered 403. Both now throw one shape.

## What changes

- **`last-admin-guard.ts`:** a new module-private `readFault()` beside `refuse()`: `code: 'SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE'` (typed `StandardErrorCode`, an existing ADR-0112 member, no new code), `status: 503`, `object` = the table the caller was writing, `cause` = the read's own failure. `failClosed` and the slug-capture rule's `catch` both throw it, with their messages unchanged. Both now pass an inner read fault through unchanged as well as an inner refusal (`judgeOrganizationDelete` nests one `failClosed` inside another), so the fault is never wrapped twice.
- **Refusals on the merits stay 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`, byte for byte.** That includes the `maxScan` overflow: that read completed and proved too large, so it is a refusal with a remedy, not a read fault.
- **`objectql-adapter.ts` (the better-auth door):** `rethrowAsBetterAuthError` gains an arm for an engine error that declares `code: 'SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE'` **and** `status: 503`, answering `APIError('SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE')` with that code and a fixed message (the driver's text is not relayed, as `mapDataError`'s declared-5xx relay withholds it). Without this arm the 503 reached better-call's router as an unhandled fault: measured by reverting only this file, `organization/update` answered **500 with no code**. The arm is keyed on the declared pair, not on the guard, so any engine error declaring that pair gets the answer `/data` already gives it.
- **`auth-manager-actor-guards.ts` (`organization/delete`):** the Default Organization's standing judge mapped only `PERMISSION_DENIED`. It now maps the guard's read fault to `APIError('SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE')` with `ORGANIZATION_DELETE_READ_FAULT_CODE`, the code that admission's own read faults (#25059) already answer with, and a message that does not relay the driver's text.

The expected landing was `last-admin-guard.ts`. The two other files are in the same package (`@objectstack/plugin-auth`) and are the doors the guard's refusal crosses: without them, the code moves at the engine and the `/data` door but the better-auth doors answer 500.

## Security floor

No change turns a refusal into an allow. Every changed site still throws, from the same place, before any write. Only the code and status of a fail-closed refusal move (403 to 503). The pins below assert that nothing was written in each fault case (`bannedFlag`, `userExists`, `memberRole`, `slugOf`, and no attempted write on `organization/delete`).

## Pins (all assert `code` + `status`)

- **HTTP door, `organization/update`** (`single-reslug-default-anchor.test.ts`): a failed read of the Default Organization now answers `{ status: 503, code: 'SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE' }` (was 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`), the body does not contain the injected driver text, and the slug is unchanged. That is the code `auth-manager.ts`'s organization slug guard answers its own read fault with (`auth-manager.org-slug-guard-system-context.test.ts`).
- **Engine door, system-context update:** the same fault gives `{ code: 'SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE', status: 503 }`.
- **Flipped** in `last-admin-guard.test.ts`: the ban, user-delete and role-downgrade fail-closed cases now assert `{ code: 'SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE', status: 503 }`. Their message assertions (the reason, "could not be verified") are unchanged.
- **New:** the `maxScan` overflow keeps `{ code: 'PERMISSION_DENIED', status: 403 }`; `judgeOrganizationDelete` with a failed inner read answers the read fault once (one `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE:` prefix); and `organization/delete` of the Default Organization through the real guard answers 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` with nothing attempted. Its CONTROL, with the read back, is the guard's verdict on the same door: 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`.
- **Repo sweep for pins on the old shape:** `git grep` for the guard's fail-closed prose and for tests driving the guard through a failing read found pins only in `plugin-auth`: the 5 flipped above. No doc or ADR states the read-fault code.

## Verification

- Reverse check, run against `main`'s three source files (`git restore --source=d12e650` on those files only, then restored from HEAD with `git diff HEAD` empty): **7 failed / 137 passed** across the four touched test files, every new or flipped pin red. Adapter alone reverted: the HTTP pin reads `expected { status: 500, code: null }`.
- `@objectstack/plugin-auth` full suite at 3aee1981: **187/187 files, 3528 passed, 10 skipped**. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth typecheck` (src, examples, test-typecheck): exit 0.
- Derived gate families (`dispatch-gates.mjs --commands`, reconciled with `--ran`): 69 derived, 67 run with exit 0, 0 unrun. Two came back NOT MEASURED locally and are left to CI: `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` needs history this shallow clone does not have, and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` needs a full monorepo build.

## Acceptance notes

- The adapter arm also gives every other engine error that declares `{ status: 503, code: 'SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE' }` the 503 answer at the better-auth door, where it used to be an empty 500. That is the same answer `mapDataError` gives on `/data`. The other in-repo producers of that pair found by `git grep` (`objectql/src/action-activation.ts`, `service-automation/src/engine.ts`) are action and flow paths, not adapter writes; this was read, not measured.
